title: Gates: batch gate and remote gate
summary: Theme Dossier for deterministic validation, consolidating AGT-W36 batch gate, AGT-W18 remote gate target architecture and AGT-W2 async validation into one current record. Section 3 keeps the batch gate in full: closed manifest and typed eligibility, mechanical replay with conflict ejection and a cascade guard, one full suite on an exact combined candidate, fenced fast-forward publication, per-member gate and integration evidence under the AGT-2543 honest-completion invariant, red classification with bounded halving and its honest-bounds table, two-level fencing and a shared ref-mutation lease with the candidate-SHA promotion train, and the operator's review-first amendment of 2026-08-18. Section 4 keeps the remote gate target: requirements R1 to R6, the GateSubject, GateAttempt, GateLease, GatePlan and GateReport contract, the central state machine, the materialization sequence, the fail-closed timeout and fallback policy with no in-process backend fallback, and the open migration behind AGT-2262. Section 5 keeps the async-validation principles that survived measurement: model-based test selection rejected, per-SHA gate cache and deterministic diff-to-project scoping recommended, staging lane measure-first. Section 10 is an evidence appendix with the AGT-W28 847-task pipeline time economy baseline and the AGT-W29 reissue-convergence negative result in one paragraph each. Ten open decisions D1 to D10 as inline decision blocks; four implementation slices. Sources recorded as superseded by this key; AGT-W28, AGT-W29 and AGT-W30 remain historical.

implementationTasks.title: Per-SHA gate cache: bind the gate verdict to the tested tree SHA and skip an unchanged re-run
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Per-SHA gate cache

Source of truth: `docs/operations/gates/index.html` (AGT-W59) section 5, and the AGT-W28 baseline in section 10. This slice is independent of the batch gate and of the remote gate ownership decision; build it first because it pays off under every option.

Deliver:

1. A durable gate-result cache keyed by the exact tested tree SHA plus the gate-profile digest. A gate request whose key already has a recorded verdict resolves from the cache instead of running the suite, and the cached verdict is reported with the original run's evidence path and original timestamp, never as a fresh run.
2. An explicit miss on any change to the gate profile, the pipeline definition version, or the toolchain identity recorded in the original run. A cache entry is never reused across profile digests.
3. A typed cache-hit classification in the pipeline step record and in the activity feed, so a reviewer can always tell a cached pass from an executed pass. A cached verdict must never be presented as a new execution.
4. Bounded retention and an invalidation path an operator can trigger per project.
5. Measurement: emit the same-SHA re-test rate (how often an identical tree is revalidated) as a reportable number, because AGT-W59 D10 needs it and it has never been measured.
6. Tests: hit, miss on profile change, miss on toolchain change, concurrent request for the same key, and a test proving a cached pass is classified distinctly from an executed pass.
7. Docs: the cache in the pipeline domain page, and one row in docs/start/README.md if a new page is added.

Out of scope: test scoping, batching, and any change to gate ownership.

implementationTasks.title: Deterministic test scoping: diff-to-project mapping as a gate filter, zero tokens
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Deterministic test scoping

Source of truth: `docs/operations/gates/index.html` (AGT-W59) section 5. Model-based test selection is recorded as explicitly rejected and must not be introduced.

Deliver:

1. A maintained folder-to-test-project mapping, declared in configuration next to the pipeline step definitions rather than hard-coded, that turns a changed-file list into the set of affected test projects.
2. Gate filter behaviour: run the mapped projects, always run every newly added test file (status A in the diff), and fall back to the full suite when the change set spans modules or when any changed path has no mapping entry. An unmapped path is a full-suite trigger, never a silent skip.
3. A test-selection audit digest recorded with the gate verdict, so a later reader can tell exactly which subset ran and why. This digest is the same field the AGT-W59 section 6 gate subject reserves.
4. A staleness guard: a check that fails loudly when a source directory exists with no mapping entry, because a stale map yields falsely green gates.
5. Tests including a case that proves an unmapped new directory forces the full suite.
6. Docs: the mapping contract and its upkeep owner in the pipeline domain page.

Out of scope: any model call, batching, and caching (separate slice).

implementationTasks.title: Claimable gate step: GateSubject, GateAttempt, lease and fenced report, with the build and test gate migrated behind a canary
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Claimable remote gate step

Source of truth: `docs/operations/gates/index.html` (AGT-W59) section 4, and open decisions D7, D8 and D9 in section 9. Do not start this slice before the operator records D7, D8 and D9; the recommended defaults are option A in each.

Deliver:

1. Task Server contract: `GateSubject`, `GateAttempt`, `GateLease`, `GatePlan` and `GateReport` with exactly the required facts and invariants in the section 6 contract table of the Dossier. The subject is immutable after creation and idempotent from source run, gate id and plan hash. At most one live fenced attempt exists per subject and gate policy.
2. Central state machine: queued, claimed, materializing, running, reporting, cleaning, and the terminals passed, product-failed, infra-retry, infra-failed, timed-out, cancelled. All state is durable across a restart.
3. Agent Host executor: claims only with fresh gate, repository and toolchain capabilities and a free gate slot; fetches the declared result ref or the digest-pinned source bundle; never scans host repositories by glob; verifies repository identity, object type and that HEAD equals the expected SHA; records tree and dirty proof; runs the frozen plan under per-command and overall deadlines; cleans up; submits a fenced report. Reuse the Review Workspace materialization, containment namespace, command evidence and cleanup primitives; do not reuse the ReviewAttempt lifecycle.
4. Orchestrator Engine: creates the subject and dispatches the stage through the public Task API and owns no durable attempt state.
5. Fail-closed classification with distinct tested outcomes for product failure, queue timeout, execution timeout, lost lease, missing snapshot, tool failure and cleanup failure. A spent retry budget terminalizes as GateInfra. No in-process fallback on the Task Server or Studio backend.
6. Report validation: stale-fence and duplicate-conflicting reports are rejected; an infrastructure retry preserves the immutable subject and raises the fence.
7. Studio read model: queue age, active host and phase, attempt count, deadline, tested SHA, terminal outcome and evidence availability derived from Task Server facts. Remove the backend's alias-based gate-count inference from the surface in the same change.
8. Migrate the post-build-test gate onto the new path behind a default-off switch, then prove a bounded canary covering remote pass, product failure, host loss, Task Server restart, Engine restart, no eligible host and cleanup failure, plus throughput parity with the current bridge.
9. Tests for every classification and for restart recovery.

Out of scope: removing the SSH bridge. AGT-2262 stays parked until the canary and restart matrix is green and the new path is the default; that teardown is its own card.

implementationTasks.title: Batch gate pilot: closed manifest, exact combined candidate, per-member evidence and bounded red isolation, documentation-only first
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Batch gate pilot

Source of truth: `docs/operations/gates/index.html` (AGT-W59) section 3, and open decisions D1 to D6 in section 9. Do not start this slice before the operator records D1 to D6 and before D10's measurement exists; the recommended defaults are option A in each.

Deliver:

1. Closed manifest: eligibility exactly as the Dossier states (settled envelope with immutable result ref, result SHA, run attempt, delivery epoch and fencing token; per-card model review passed on that subject with the build and test aspect recorded as deferred-to-batch; current generation with no newer attempt, reissue or supersede; matching project, repository, integration branch, gate profile and platform version; not owned by another batch or an active per-task gate). Record every eligible key and every exclusion with a typed reason. The manifest is durable before any Git work starts and never absorbs a member after close.
2. Deterministic order and a membership digest over order, base SHA, member subjects and gate profile, carried on every state write and candidate ref.
3. Mechanical replay into disposable detached worktrees with the existing conflict-free rebase rules, a replacement-to-original SHA mapping per member, typed ejection of a conflicting member without changing the batch tip, and the conflict cascade guard (close the candidate at more than a quarter conflicting or three in succession).
4. Green path: persist the batch-run record before execution; run the complete suite once on a clean checkout of the candidate SHA; revalidate every member generation; acquire the shared project ref-mutation lease; verify the develop tip still equals the recorded pre-tip; publish by fast-forward, or by a merge commit only if that exact commit was the tested candidate; never create an untested merge commit after the suite; verify the remote resolves to the tested candidate. A moved pre-tip is stale-base: reconstruct and rerun.
5. A native append-only per-member batch-gate record carrying task key, run attempt, delivery epoch, original result SHA, replacement SHA set, batch id, membership digest, base SHA, tested candidate SHA, gate profile digest, batch-run id, verdict and evidence path. Missing or mismatched identity is batch-gate-evidence-missing and blocks lane release. The existing integration-record endpoint keeps only its bookkeeping role.
6. Red path: classify infrastructure red, deterministic suite red and flaky red separately; one same-SHA retry on a healthy host for infrastructure red and a visible pause on the second; ordered halving capped at ceil(log2 n) diagnostic runs per cycle with an explicit unresolved-cohort fallback and a survivor rerun; the existing bounded flaky quarantine policy, never majority-vote green.
7. Authority: a durable coordinator lease keyed by project, repository, integration branch and gate profile, with publication forbidden after lease loss; the shared fenced ref-mutation lease with direct integration, auto-main advancement and the candidate-SHA promotion train, whose publish phases may not overlap; supersede handling per the four moments in the Dossier.
8. Formation triggers and gate-ordering behaviour per the recorded D1 and D6 answers, configurable per project, plus a per-project disable that stops manifest formation and returns unmirrored members to the per-task gate with the same immutable subject.
9. The predeclared pilot measurements from section 7 as reportable numbers, including the correctness floor (zero stale-attempt passes, missing SHA mappings, untested publish SHAs or false Completed cards).
10. Tests for eligibility, ordering, conflict ejection and the cascade guard, stale-base, supersede at each of the four moments, lease loss, halving bounds, and evidence-record failure blocking lane release.

Route the pilot to documentation-only deliveries first. Do not change default routing for code-bearing cards in this slice.
